COS-70.3-Q2.why: Withheld, so there is no substantive answer. The sources it consulted were 82.1051, not the key's 70.3(j), (k), (l) and (m) definitions of lake, mixture and diluent.

COS-70.10-Q1.why: Withheld, so there is no substantive answer. It never states the 70.10(b)(1)-(3) NDA color-additive rules (part 71 safety data, inferential proposal, filing date).

COS-70.11-Q1.why: Answers yes and correctly restates 70.11(a)-(d): additive toxic effects are presumed for color additives, food additives and pesticides, and (d) considers common components and similar biological activity. The headline's 'as long as' condition is loose, but the body restates (d) correctly.

COS-70.19-Q1.why: Withheld. It does not give the $2,600 deposit or the withdrawal refunds and resubmission fees in 70.19(c)-(h).

COS-70.20-Q1.why: States every 70.20 element correctly: containers that prevent changes in composition, a seal that must be broken to open, the moisture-change carve-out, and food-additive packaging authorized under parts 170-189. The 70.3(j) citation is correct. It omits the hair-dye exclusion, which is not relevant here, and frames the rules as 'permitted' (minor).

COS-70.45-Q1.why: Withheld, and the sources consulted were 740.10, which is unrelated. There is no answer on 70.45 allocation of the safe tolerance, the Federal Register call for data or the stayed time limit.

COS-71.4-Q1.why: Covers all 71.4 elements: FDA may request samples and information and must state the quantity, the 90-day limit moves forward one day per day of delay, and the petition counts as withdrawn without prejudice if samples are not submitted within 180 days. 'Must provide' is slightly strong, but the withdrawal consequence is stated correctly.

COS-71.6-Q2.why: Correctly answers yes under 71.6(c)(1): withdrawal is without prejudice and the time limit runs anew on refiling. It also gives (c)(2), withdrawal any time before the order goes to the Federal Register. Both citations are correct.

COS-71.20-Q1.why: Covers the 90/180-day timing, listing in part 73 or 74, the (a)(1) conditions, (a)(2) listing only uses found safe or else denial, (a)(3) and the (b) certification exemption. All citations are correct. It says 'published' where the rule says 'forwarded for publication', a minor slip.

COS-71.22-Q1.why: Withheld, and the sources consulted were 73.2329. It fails to say no under 71.22: a general listing does not authorize use that conceals damage or inferiority.

COS-71.30-Q1.why: Withheld even though 71.30(a) and (b) were retrieved. It does not point to parts 10, 12-16 and 19 for objections and hearings, or to the 70.19 fees.

COS-71.37-Q1.why: Correct exemption label statement and correct 71.37(b) records (expert's name and address, date, quantity, batch or code mark, 2 years, available for inspection). Minor slips: 'delivered by experts' should be 'to experts', and the exempted sections 402(c), 501(a) and 601(e) are not named.

COS-73.2087-Q1.why: Cites (a), (b), (c)(1), (c)(2), (d) and 70.3(s) correctly and covers every key element. But it misreads the labeling rule: it says labeling applies because the blush is used near the eye, then flatly states the user's blush is 'not subject to § 701.3'. That turns the (c)(2) condition into an unconditional claim, and a retail blush normally is subject to 701.3.

COS-73.2110-Q1.why: Correct on the 2.0% (w/v) cap, scalp-only use ((c)(1)-(2)), the full (d)(2) warning text and the (e) certification exemption. It leaves out (d)(1), the § 70.25 labeling requirement for the additive, which is a key element.

COS-73.2120-Q1.why: Answer was withheld and gives no substance. It never says the additive is permitted only in shampoos and not in body wash, and gives none of the (d)/(e) requirements.

COS-73.2150-Q1.why: Says the use is permitted and that there is no numeric cap (GMP only). Correctly cites and quotes (a) conformance to 73.1150(a)(1) and (b), (b) externally applied cosmetics only (70.3(v) defines the term), (c) § 70.25 labeling and (d) the exemption. All key elements are present.

COS-73.2162-Q1.why: Says the use is permitted for eye shadow under (b) (cosmetics generally, eye area included, GMP, no cap). Gives (a)(1) conformance to 73.1162(a)(1) and (b), the accurate (a)(2) diluent limits, (c) § 70.25 labeling and (d) the exemption. Matches the key.

COS-73.2299-Q1.why: Says the use is permitted under (b) (externally applied cosmetics, eye area included, GMP, no cap). Gives (a) conformance to 73.1299(a)(1) and (b), (c) § 70.25 labeling and (d) the exemption, with correct definitions. Matches the key.

COS-73.2326-Q1.why: Says the use is permitted for an eye pencil under (b) (externally applied cosmetics, eye area included, GMP, no cap). Gives (a) conformance to 73.1326(a)(1) and (b), (c) § 70.25 labeling and (d) the exemption. Matches the key.

COS-73.2329-Q1.why: Citations and coverage of (a)(1), (b), (c) and (d) are correct. But the opening makes use conditional on the product being 'externally applied' and containing only 73.1001(b) diluents. Guanine is permitted in cosmetics generally, and the (a)(2)(ii) diluent limit applies to color additive mixtures, not the whole nail polish, so the requirement's scope is misstated in a way that could mislead.

COS-73.2400-Q1.why: Says the use is permitted for body powder under (b) (externally applied cosmetics, GMP, no cap). Gives (a) conformance to 73.1400(a)(1) and (b), (c) § 70.25 labeling, (d) the exemption and the 70.3(v) definition. Matches the key.

COS-73.2496-Q1.why: Says the use is permitted under (b) (cosmetics generally, eye area included, GMP, no cap). Gives (a) conformance to 73.1496(a)(1) and (b), (c) § 70.25 labeling and (d) the exemption. Matches the key.

COS-73.2775-Q1.why: Says lipstick use is permitted under (c) (cosmetics generally, GMP). Quotes the (b) specifications, including lead 20 ppm, arsenic 3 ppm, mercury 1 ppm and total color 93% or more, plus (d) § 70.25 labeling and (e) the exemption. Covers (a)-(e) as the key requires.

COS-74.2101-Q1.why: Answer was withheld, and the sources it consulted were for the wrong section (74.2340). It never states the (c)(1)/(c)(2) permissions or the (e) batch certification requirement.

COS-74.2104-Q1.why: Says the body lotion use is permitted under 74.2104(b) with no numeric limit beyond GMP, and backs that with 70.3(v). It covers certification under part 80 (74.2104(d)) and labeling per 70.25 (74.2104(c)). The extra citations (74.2104(a), 82.1104, 82.1050) are correct.

COS-74.2151-Q1.why: Says the hand cream use is permitted under 74.2151(c) with a GMP amount and no numeric limit, and gives 70.3(v) as the external-use basis. It covers certification (74.2151(e)) and the label per 70.25 (74.2151(d)). The quotes from (a) and (b) are accurate extras.

COS-74.2205-Q1.why: Correctly finds that both the mascara and the body wash are permitted, since 74.2205(b) covers cosmetics generally including the eye area under current GMP. It covers certification (74.2205(d)) and labeling (74.2205(c)). Writing 'good manufacturing practice' in place of 'current GMP' is a minor slip.

COS-74.2206-Q1.why: Says the foot cream use is permitted under 74.2206(b) with a GMP amount and no numeric limit, with 70.3(v) as the basis. It covers certification (74.2206(d)) and the 70.25 label (74.2206(c)). The 82.1206 restriction to external use is an accurate extra.

COS-74.2255-Q1.why: Applies the right limit to each product: lipstick up to 5.0% by weight, and mouthwash (as an ingested cosmetic) and body lotion in GMP amounts. This matches 74.2255(b), which it quotes in full. It also gives (c) labeling and (d) certification. The 82.1255(b) citation used for mouthwash and lotion is a real provision whose text supports those claims.

COS-74.2260-Q1.why: Gets permitted use, the GMP amount and the 70.3(v) basis right. However, it quotes 74.2260(d) as printed ('D&C Orange No. 11') without flagging the misprint, and it never says plainly that D&C Orange No. 10 needs certification. The certification answer is left ambiguous, and the key's misprint element is missing.

COS-74.2328-Q1.why: Correctly says the nail lacquer is permitted under 74.2328(b), which covers cosmetics generally under current GMP. It correctly says the eyeliner is not permitted, because under 70.5(a) a listing must specifically provide for eye-area use (with 70.3(s) defining that area). It covers certification (74.2328(d)) and labeling (74.2328(c)).

COS-74.2330-Q1.why: Correctly says the lip liner is permitted under 74.2330(b), which covers cosmetics generally. It correctly says the eye shadow is not authorized under 70.5(a), with 70.3(s) for the eye area. It covers certification (74.2330(d)) and the 70.25 label (74.2330(c)), matching the key.

COS-74.2331-Q1.why: Says the body butter use is permitted under 74.2331(b) with a GMP amount and no numeric limit, with 70.3(v) as the basis. It covers certification (74.2331(d)) and labeling (74.2331(c)). All citations are correct.

COS-74.2334-Q1.why: Says the body lotion use is permitted under 74.2334(b) with no numeric limit beyond GMP, with 70.3(v) as the basis. It covers certification (74.2334(d)) and the 70.25 label (74.2334(c)). The 82.1334 identity and specification quotes are extras that do no harm.

COS-74.2602-Q1.why: Says the hand cream use is permitted under 74.2602(b) with a GMP amount and no numeric limit, with 70.3(v) as the basis. It covers certification (74.2602(d)) and labeling (74.2602(c)), matching every element of the key.

COS-74.2707-Q1.why: Says the body scrub use is permitted under 74.2707(b) with a GMP amount and no numeric limit, with 70.3(v) as the basis. It covers certification (74.2707(d)) and the 70.25 label (74.2707(c)). All citations are correct.

COS-80.22-Q1.why: Covers 80.22(a), (b) and all five (c) label/labeling items with correct paragraph citations. However, the closing line ('the requirement that the batch be thoroughly mixed ... applies only if the batch has been properly mixed') invents a circular condition that recasts the unconditional mixing requirement as conditional.

COS-80.34-Q1.why: All four 80.34(a)(1)-(4) grounds and the 80.34(b) part 16 hearing are stated correctly with correct citations. It omits that suspension can be immediate and lasts until adequate corrective action is taken, which is a key 'what can we do' element.

COS-80.39-Q1.why: Correctly states the (b)(1) use and (b)(2) shipment record contents, the (c) separate-keeping rule and the (a) 2-years-after-disposal availability to FDA/HHS officers, all cited to the right paragraphs. The FDA opportunity to inventory stocks is not mentioned, but that is peripheral to what records and how long.

COS-81.10-Q1.why: Reaches the correct conclusions (lipstick not permitted per 70.3(v), body lotion permitted at GMP under 74.2304, 82.304 restricted to external use), and every citation given is correct. It never surfaces the primary key provision 81.10(d) or the termination of the provisional listing for food, ingested drugs and ingested cosmetics.

COS-82.3-Q1.why: Withheld; neither the 82.3(i) gloss white definition nor the 82.3(n) externally applied definition was delivered, and the foot cream was not addressed.

COS-82.5-Q1.why: Correctly gives 82.5(a) and the (b)(1) subpart B limits (Pb 0.001%, As2O3 0.00014%, other heavy metals trace), and the extra (b)(2)/(b)(3) limits are correct. However, it misreads (b)(1)(iii) by adding an invented GMP-avoidability condition to the 'not more than trace' limit.

COS-82.51-Q1.why: All citations are correct: 82.51(a)(1), (a)(2), (b), (b)(1)-(3) and 82.50. Composition, previously certified colors, the 2.0% chlorides/sulfates limit and the naming rule all match the key. Two problems keep sub at 1. First, the single specification 'inorganic matter, insoluble in HCl, not more than 0.5%' is garbled into 'insoluble HCl and inorganic matter', and the summary just says 'limits on inorganic matter'. Read literally, that caps all inorganic matter, which is wrong for an alumina lake. Second, the summary says lakes must meet the parent color's specifications 'including those in §82.50', which the regulation does not say. So this is not a full PASS.

COS-82.705-Q1.why: Delivered only a verbatim quote of 82.705 (conform to 74.705(a)(1) and (b)) and 82.50 (conform to 82.5), with correct citations. It does not apply them or state the 82.5 subpart B limits (Pb 0.001%, As2O3 0.00014%, heavy metals trace) that the key requires.

COS-82.706-Q1.why: Cites only 82.50 and 70.3(j). It omits the primary provision 82.706 and its requirement to conform to 74.706(a)(1) and (b), and never states the 82.5 limits, so it does not say what specifications apply.

COS-82.1255-Q1.why: Correctly gives 82.1255(a) identity per 74.1255(a)(1) and (b), and (b) at most 5.0% for lip products and GMP amounts for dentifrices, mouthwashes and externally applied cosmetics. It also correctly notes neither product is 'externally applied' under 70.3(v), and cites 82.1050 correctly.

COS-82.1328-Q1.why: Withheld with no substantive content. It does not state the 74.1328(a)(1)/(b) conformance requirement, the absence of any use restriction, or the 82.1050 drugs-and-cosmetics-only certification.

COS-82.1330-Q1.why: Verbatim quotes of 82.1330 and 82.1050 with correct citations. It never answers the 'does it set limits' part (the key says 82.1330 sets no use restriction or quantitative limit), so the provision is restated without being applied.

COS-82.1331-Q1.why: Correctly answers 'not permitted' for lip liner. It cites 82.1331's restriction to externally applied products and 70.3(v)'s exclusion of the lips, and states the 74.1331(a)(1) and (b) conformity requirement. The extra 74.2331 and 82.1050 citations are accurate.

COS-82.1334-Q1.why: All key specifications are given correctly and cited to 82.1334: identity, volatiles/chlorides/sulfates at most 15%, the amine at most 0.2%, 3-hydroxy-2-naphthoic acid at most 0.4%, subsidiary colors at most 4%, total color at least 85%. The 'azol' typo does not change the requirement, and the 82.1050 addition is accurate.

COS-82.1336-Q1.why: The answer carries a 'could not be validated' notice but quotes 82.1336(a) and (b) verbatim, which is exactly what the question asked for. It gives the color's conformity to 74.1336(a)(1) and (b) and that lakes must be made from previously certified batches. The citations are correct.

COS-82.1602-Q1.why: It restates 82.1602 and 82.1050 correctly but never answers 'does it restrict use?'. The key's point that 82.1602 states no use restriction or quantitative limit is missing, and the 82.1050 'use only in drugs and cosmetics' wording is left uninterpreted.

COS-82.2051-Q1.why: The (a)(2) specifications and the (b) naming rule are correct, but the (a)(1) summary is garbled. It omits the requirement that the straight color be a sodium, potassium, barium or calcium salt (or a salt made with the listed radicals). It also truncates the substrata list and frames the answer confusingly ('permitted... not restricted by the substrate alone').

COS-82.2707a-Q1.why: Correctly says permitted for a hand cream under 82.2707a's externally-applied restriction and 70.3(v). It gives conformity to 74.1707a(a)(1) and (b) and says no percentage limit is stated. Minor slip: the 74.2707a(b) quote drops 'Ext.', which does not change the requirement.

COS-700.3-Q2.why: This is the 'could not be validated' fallback: it dumps all of 700.3 verbatim and never answers the yes/no question. Definitions (e) and (h) are present, but the key's 'yes to both' is never stated, so the answer only quotes text.

COS-700.11-Q1.why: Correctly answers no, at any level: under 700.11(a) bithionol is a deleterious substance and any cosmetic containing it is adulterated. It also correctly states the photosensitization and cross-sensitization rationale and the 700.11(b) proceedings for products shipped after March 15, 1968. Citations are correct to the paragraph.

COS-700.23-Q1.why: The 'No' is correct and properly cited to 700.23. It never surfaces 2.125(b), (c) or (e), so the key's explanation is absent: a cosmetic aerosol is not an essential use unless listed in (e), and (e) lists none.

COS-700.25-Q1.why: The 'yes' and the (b) and (c) obligations are mostly right, but it says 'the requirement does not apply to aerosol products', citing (b). In (b), an aerosol container is an example of 'distinctive by design'; the aerosol exception covers only the (c) labeling statement. The vaginal-tablet date is cited to (e)(1)(i)/(e)(2), not (e)(1)(ii), and the (a) adulteration/misbranding consequence is missing.

COS-700.25-Q3.why: The later (e)(1) and (e)(2) lines give the correct dates. But the main bullet says the labeling-statement requirement took effect February 6, 1984 (correct: May 5, 1983), and the summary wrongly ties labeling dates to product type. That internal contradiction would mislead an auditor.

COS-700.27-Q2.why: It correctly states the (c)(6) entry affirmation and the duty to produce records within 5 days if requested, plus the (c)(1) recordkeeping duty and (c)(2) 2-year retention. The added definitions are accurate. Minor slip: it attributes the records request to CBP.

COS-700.27-Q3.why: Withheld. Nothing was answered and no citation was given, so the key's 'No' under 700.27(a)(4), (a)(1) and (b)(1) was never delivered.

COS-701.1-Q1.why: Cites 701.1(b) correctly and gets the direction right ('may be misleading'). But it misreads the facts, saying not all ingredients are listed, and misreads the rule as covering named ingredients that are 'not all included in the product'. It also calls the practice 'prohibited', where the key stresses the section only says 'may be' misleading.

COS-701.2-Q1.why: Correct 'Yes', with 701.2(a)(6) properly applied to small type and poor background contrast. It omits 701.2(a)(1), failure to appear on the part of the label presented under customary conditions of purchase, which is the key element for printing on the jar bottom.

COS-701.3-Q3.why: Gives only the common-brand condition of (g)(2)(iii). It omits (g)(2)(i) same-use similar products, (ii) the shaded 720.4(c)(3) category and (iv) the color-additive limit, and it omits (g)(1) entirely. It frames 'may contain' as allowed for any ingredient not present, and wrongly says no provision addresses colorants, although (g) does exactly that.

COS-701.9-Q2.why: For an own-plant shipment the key is 701.9(b): the exemption is void from the start of removal for the misbranded part. The answer rests mainly on 701.9(d)(1), which covers (a)(2) agreement shipments and says 'expire', not void ab initio. It also says the exemption depends on a written agreement, which an own-plant shipment does not need, and invents a trigger for mislabeling 'during movement or holding'.

COS-701.11-Q1.why: It opens by saying flatly that 'Midnight Muse' is not sufficient and then contradicts itself. The key says the name works if the product's nature is obvious. The bold-type and size requirement is cited to 701.11(a) but is in (c), and (b)(1) is misstated as 'shall be used'.

COS-701.13-Q2.why: Withheld. It does not say the product is not exempt, and it does not give the 701.13(e)(1) tear-away tag/tape PDP rule or the (f)(1) 5 sq in waiver.

COS-701.20-Q1.why: Declines and never surfaces 701.20(a)/(b), which define soap and make a syndet bar a cosmetic. It cites irrelevant 720.4 provisions and turns the voluntary Form 2512 'should' items into requirements ('requires'), which counts as invented requirements.

COS-710.3-Q1.why: Accurately describes 710.3: Form FD-2511, where to obtain it and where to mail it. It omits the key element that this is a voluntary program FDA stopped accepting in March 2023, and calls FD-2511 'the required form', which could mislead a user into treating it as a current, mandatory registration route.

COS-710.7-Q1.why: Correct 'Yes'. It cites 710.7 and correctly states that a copy of the filed FD-2511 is available for inspection at FDA, 5001 Campus Dr., College Park, MD, matching the key.

COS-710.8-Q1.why: Reaches 'No' on the wrong basis: that 710.6 does not authorize the statement. It never surfaces 710.8, under which registration or a registration number does not denote FDA approval and any representation creating that impression is misleading.

COS-710.9-Q1.why: The answer was withheld and replaced with verbatim quotes of 710.9(a)-(c) and 700.3(b), all cited correctly. It never says the spa is not requested to register, and it omits the 710.9 introductory text that gives (a) its effect, so the question goes unanswered.

COS-720.1-Q1.why: 720.1 and 700.3(b) are cited correctly, but the answer turns 720.1's voluntary request into a mandatory duty ('is required to file', 'is responsible for filing') and suggests the distributor is the one obligated, when the key says any of manufacturer, packer or distributor may file. It also leaves out that no filing fee is required.

COS-720.2-Q1.why: Declines to answer and never surfaces 720.2. The key element (file within 60 days after commercial distribution begins) is missing.

COS-720.4-Q2.why: Answers with the 720.6 amendment and discontinuance timing instead of the question asked. None of the 720.4(b) elements appear: providing the (a) information, an authorized signature, ingredient information for poison control centers, and ingredient information or samples for treating physicians.

COS-720.6-Q1.why: Correctly gives 60 days after commercial distribution for the ingredient and brand-name changes under 720.6. But it wrongly says the office move needs no action, when 720.6 says other changes such as the address should be shown on an amended Form 2512 within one year.

COS-740.2-Q1.why: Withheld, so no substantive answer. The 740.2(a) prominence, bold-type, contrasting-background and 1/16-inch requirements are never stated.

COS-740.10-Q2.why: Correctly states all three conjunctive 740.10(b) conditions under which the warning is not required, with correct (a) and (b) citations. It omits 740.10(c): this is not an exemption from the Act's adulteration provisions or any other requirement.

COS-740.17-Q1.why: The first paragraph gives the full 740.17(b) caution and the optional 'except under adult supervision' wording from (c). The second paragraph then says this kids' product must bear a shortened caution ('Use only as directed. Keep out of reach of children'), which contradicts the first and misstates the required warning.

COS-740.18-Q1.why: Correctly quotes the 740.18(a) warning text and the (b) ingredients, including the sulfate. But it never says the section was stayed until further notice effective Sept. 18, 1980 (47 FR 7829), and it states the product 'is subject to the warning requirement'. That answers the 'is it in effect' question wrongly.

COS-FDCA601-Q1.why: Withheld, and FD&C Act 601(a) is never surfaced. The hair-dye caution text and the preliminary-test directions are missing.

COS-FDCA601-Q2.why: Withheld. Its sources were 700.27, not FD&C Act 601(b)-(d), and none of the filth, insanitary-conditions or poisonous-container provisions are stated.

COS-FDCA602-Q1.why: Correctly gives all three 602(b) package-form label elements (name/place of business, accurate net quantity, 609/364e information) with the reasonable-variation and small-package regulatory exemptions, cited to 602(b). The first paragraph slightly blends variations with small-package exemptions, but the second states them correctly.

COS-FDCA604-Q2.why: Applies the facts: a second-degree burn is significant disfigurement under customary use, so it is a serious adverse event (604(5)). Responsible person is defined correctly per 604(4) with the 609(a)/15 U.S.C. 1453(a) label reference. The pinpoint '604(5)(vii)' leaves out the (A) level but points to the correct paragraph and clause.

COS-FDCA605-Q2.why: Gives the 6-year retention, the 3-year period for small businesses not making 612(b) products, and inspection access for credentialed, duly designated HHS officers or employees, all cited to 605(e). Calling small businesses 'exempt' is a wording slip, but the stated 3-year period is correct.

COS-FDCA608-Q1.why: Cites '608(c)(3)', which does not exist; the cumulative-exposure text sits in 608(c)(2). The (c)(1) paraphrase drops the governing 'sufficient to support a reasonable certainty that the product is safe' standard. The answer also omits that a product lacking substantiation is adulterated under 601(g), a key element.

COS-FDCA610-Q1.why: Core obligation matches 610(a): credentials and written notice, reasonable times and manner, access to and copying of records on the product and similarly affected products needed for the adulteration and threat determination. However, the data-exclusion list (610(b)) and the 'solely labeling/holding/distributing facility' carve-out (604(3)(B)) are both cited to 610(a), the wrong paragraph.

COS-FDCA610-Q2.why: Correctly answers yes, conditioned on the Secretary's reasonable belief of adulteration posing a serious-harm threat, applying to 'each responsible person and facility'. It cites 610(a), 604(4) and 604(3)(B) correctly, and its exclusions are accurate. But it never says what the duty actually requires: letting a designated officer access and copy records relating to the product and to other similarly affected products, as needed to assist the Secretary. That key element matters for a contract filler that makes products for several brands, so this is not a PASS.

COS-FDCA611-Q1.why: Misreads 611(a). The answer says FDA may order cessation 'or recall' 'even if' the person refuses, but the key says the responsible person must first get a chance to stop distribution and recall voluntarily. Only if it refuses or fails to act in time can FDA order distribution stopped, and recall comes by amended order after the hearing under 611(c), which the answer skips. The 10-day hearing in 611(b) is correct.

COS-FDCA612-Q2.why: Declined ('no amount is given') and listed 613/604(3) as sources. It never identifies the $800,000 three-year average of U.S. cosmetic sales under 612(a) as the relevant figure, or the 612(b) condition.

COS-FDCA614-Q1.why: Correctly states that under 614(a) no State may establish or continue registration and product-listing requirements different from, in addition to, or not identical with federal ones, and applies this to facility registration without opining on a specific state law. The hedge about non-registration requirements does not misstate the rule.

UC-COS-024.why: Correctly covers 700.27(c)(1) records, 2-year retention, the importer's 5-day production of records, and the absence of any quarantine requirement. But the summary says records must show the tallow is under 0.15% insoluble impurities AND from non-prohibited tissue, when (a)(6) says OR. It also omits the record-location and FDA inspection-and-copying requirements in (c), and the 700.27(d)/601(c) adulteration consequence.

UC-COS-002.why: Answer withheld; no substantive response. Misses 610 records access (SAHCOD belief, credentials and written notice), the personnel-data exclusion with its exception for technical and professional qualifications, and 704.

UC-COS-004.why: Correctly says no FDA certification is needed, but gives no citation and then contradicts itself by declining. Omits that 606 GMP rules have not been issued, that FDA does not certify equipment, and the 601(c)/601(a) insanitary-conditions and deleterious-substance duties.

UC-COS-005.why: Plain decline with no citation. It does not say the regulation is silent on calibration frequency and records, and does not mention 606 GMP status as the key requires.
